subject: Biology
title: Neurons: The Body's Wiring
description: A quick, practical guide to Neurons: The Body's Wiring.

hook.text: Neurons transmit electrical signals at speeds up to 120 meters per second.

buildup.text: Each neuron has a cell body, branching dendrites, and a long axon that sends signals.

discovery.text: Signals jump between neurons at synapses, using chemical neurotransmitters.

twist.text: Your brain holds about 86 billion neurons, each connecting to thousands of others.

climax.text: Every thought, memory, and movement starts as an impulse racing through neurons.

punchline.text: Electricity and chemistry—that's how you think.

quiz.question: How do signals cross from one neuron to the next?

details.summary: Neurons are electrically excitable cells that transmit signals throughout the nervous system. Their unique shape, with dendrites for receiving signals, a cell body for integration, and a long axon for transmission, makes them the body's specialized communication wiring.
details.whyItMatters: Neurons enable every sensation, thought, and movement. Their specialization for rapid signal transmission over long distances explains how the brain controls the body and processes information in milliseconds.
takeaways: Neurons are specialized for rapid electrical signal transmission
Sensory neurons carry information to the brain; motor neurons carry commands out
Most adult neurons do not divide, making brain injuries difficult to repair

faq.question: Why can't the brain repair itself like skin does?
faq.answer: Most mature neurons have permanently exited the cell cycle and cannot divide. While limited neurogenesis occurs in two brain regions, it is insufficient for major repair. This is why spinal cord injuries and stroke damage are often permanent.

faq.question: How long can a single neuron be?
faq.answer: Motor neurons controlling your toes have cell bodies in the spinal cord and axons extending to the foot, spanning over a meter. The giraffe's recurrent laryngeal nerve reaches nearly 5 meters, making it one of the longest cells in any animal.
